name: additional-violations-unknown-field-and-immutable-field
description: One change set carrying three independent violations, all found by pass B. It is the vector that makes `errorResult.additional` a contract rather than an unused field: the response reports the first violation in pass order as the primary and the other two alongside it, so a client fixes the whole change set in one round trip instead of learning about one violation per attempt.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model. `ExampleSWC` exists and has no `safety_level` field; `CORE0` is a hardware `core` whose `kind` discriminator discovery declares immutable; `uint16_base` is already declared in `data_types/base/`. The three operations are unrelated to each other, which is the point — none of them is a consequence of another.

authorization.notes: Every requested address is covered, so the change set clears gate 1 and the three refusals are all about the operations themselves.

input.intent: Record an ASIL level, turn CORE0 into a memory and add a 16-bit base type.

expected.notes: The primary is the FIRST violation the pass order reaches, and pass B walks the operations in the order given — so the primary is the first operation's, and `additional` carries the other two in operation order. Nothing in `additional` repeats the primary. All three are pass-B codes here, but the rule is wider: a violation found in a LATER pass that still ran is reported too, in the detection order, and only a pass that could not run at all reports nothing. `failure_class` on the result is the primary's class; every code involved is `invalid`, and every one of the four classes leaves the real model byte-identical anyway.
